CanonicalKeywords.rationale: `{ CardKeyword.Innate }` (MindBlast.cs:22) == `innate = True`. A CANONICAL Innate rather than an upgrade-added one, so no downgrade-rebuild hazard -- and it is load-bearing for the card's own damage, since Innate means it is in the opening hand while the draw pile is still large.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (MindBlast.cs:24-27) == cost 1 / ATTACK / UNCOMMON / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `CalculationBaseVar(0m)` + `ExtraDamageVar(1m)` + `CalculatedDamageVar(ValueProp.Move).WithMultiplier((card, _) => PileType.Draw.GetPile(card.Owner).Cards.Count)` (MindBlast.cs:15-20). `CalculatedVar.Calculate` is `base + extra * multiplier` (CalculatedVar.cs:62-71) = `0 + 1 * drawPileCount` == the sim's `len(ctx.player.draw_pile)`. Move without Unpowered -> powered on both sides.

OnPlay.rationale: `DamageCmd.Attack(DynamicVars.CalculatedDamage).FromCard(this).Targeting(cardPlay.Target)` (MindBlast.cs:32-34) == `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, target, self.calc_damage(ctx, target), dealer=ctx.player, card=self)`. The draw pile is counted at play time on both sides, and Mind Blast itself is never in it (Play pile in C#, discard-pile limbo in the sim).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `EnergyCost.UpgradeBy(-1)` (MindBlast.cs:39) == `self._energy_cost = max(0, self._energy_cost - 1)` (1 -> 0). The damage formula is untouched by the upgrade on both sides.
